title: Cabinet-frame relational diffusion with explicit robot/world context
coverage_gap: D20 contains ten LL and ten HH layouts: cabinet x and yaw sign co-vary. C reverses that association and E has both larger translation and roughly 35 degree yaw, versus 5-10 degree support yaw. A world-coordinate network can confound lateral reach with cabinet orientation.
reusable_regularity: Hand-to-handle approach, handle-to-goal travel and observed motion can be expressed in the rigid cabinet yaw frame. The support goal-minus-initial-handle vector is 0.128 m along negative cabinet y in demos 00-04 in the inspected summary. An orthogonal frame change removes the need to learn that rotation from the correlated support. This is an approximate action/geometry regularity, not a claim that the fixed-orientation robot or native action cube is rotationally symmetric.
dependencies_preserved: Current and embedded previous hand/handle positions yield cabinet-local relative approach, remaining travel and one-control-step displacements. Both whole causal observations are separately transformed.

Absolute world hand, handle and goal positions remain in the condition, retaining robot reach and vertical/table relationships. Raw cabinet yaw and current/previous object quaternion retain cabinet orientation versus the fixed gripper.
Current/previous aperture is retained, with no forced gripper action despite the support's constant -1 command. Object2 channels alone are omitted because the schema declares them absent zeros.
Cabinet pose and handle/goal geometry are retained; no collision-free path or unobserved obstacle state is assumed.

evidence_refs.use: Exact current drawer__N20__rep0 support identities and evidence scope.
Yaw sin/cos slices, corrected handle point, absent object2, fixed native orientation and control semantics; correlated support and extrapolation ranges.
Cell counts and inspected demo 00-04 geometry descriptors: constant 0.128 m initial handle-to-goal length along rotated negative y; action gripper mean -1 and standard deviation zero.
Stationary handle during approach, hand descent and the change to pulling; small observed-step differences compared to reach distances.
Robot, cabinet, handle and tabletop layout at reset.
Elevated approach above the closed drawer; robot geometry is world-fixed.
Open drawer and hand moving away from cabinet.
One frozen DP, two causal observations, action4-first, native executor-only clipping.

expected_failure_signature: If approximate yaw equivariance breaks at large yaw because the gripper cannot rotate, E should show correct gross approach but lateral contact loss during pull.
If the network still exploits absolute world pose, crossed C cells should show lateral approach errors despite correct local inputs.
No explicit stage bottleneck is present: near the descend-to-pull transition the model may hesitate or pull before contact. These are hypotheses, not measured outcomes.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41] only; normalized history is provided by the common host but replaced by deterministic physical features
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: For all 16 translations use R_z(yaw_at_chunk_start)^T times native world action xyz. Decode with R_z from the same raw_current yaw. Gripper stays identical. No position origin is applied to action vectors; one native action unit remains 0.01 m. No candidate clipping or horizon integration.
required_runtime_fields.scales: Relative positions /0.1 m, observed native-step displacements /0.01 m, absolute world positions relative to [0,0.6,0] /0.5 m; yaw, quaternions and aperture unstandardized. These fixed unit choices avoid amplification of near-constant support yaw cos or goal coordinates; they do not alter host normalization or action loss.

change_summary: Initial standalone geometric candidate. One common DP conditioned on 36 deterministic features, no learned auxiliary encoder or head, no support-fit state, no auxiliary loss. All native action4 epsilon loss and mask rules remain unchanged. No performance feedback was available.
